# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260920-2205-candidate-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-20 22:05 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-20 22:07 CDT`
- Research scope: Four unresolved candidate URLs for Subway and Domino's
- Queue item or vendor: Restaurant365 and Crunchtime candidate-page validation
- Methodology: Direct retrieval and page-level validation of vendor-hosted source pages

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4 candidate URLs (3 unique resources because one Restaurant365 URL redirects to the other)
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 1 low-confidence indication
- Conflicts found: 0
- Material takeaway: A Restaurant365 marketing article uses present-tense language indicating that unspecified Subway franchisees use R365 Employee Training, but it names no operator, location count, case study, or implementation. Preserve this as a 35% franchisee-scoped indication, not a confirmed Subway enterprise relationship. The two Crunchtime/Domino's candidates do not support a deployment claim: one is now a 404 and the other is a content-free registration thank-you page.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Subway
- Vendor: Restaurant365
- Product or category: R365 Employee Training, including mobile training, standardized learning paths, AI translation, progress reporting, and food-safety certification access
- Relationship indication: `unknown`
- Deployment scope: `franchisee`
- Evidence type: `other`
- Confidence: `35%`
- Confidence rationale: Restaurant365's own page says in present tense that Subway franchisees use R365 Employee Training and describes product-specific workflows. However, the page is promotional copy with a demo call-to-action, not a case study; it names no franchisee, executive, location count, contract, rollout, or independent source. The language may describe a subset of franchisees or a product marketed to them rather than a verified deployment.
- Source title: How Subway Franchisees are Building Stronger Teams with R365
- Source URL: https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/how-subway-franchisees-are-building-stronger-teams-with-r365/
- Publisher or source owner: Restaurant365
- Published date, if known: Not shown in the retrieved page
- Accessed date: `2026-09-20`
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Restaurant365 says Subway franchisees are using its Employee Training tools to reduce turnover and standardize training, then describes mobile training, customizable paths, AI-powered translation, employee-progress reporting, and Always Food Safe certification access.
- Product-specific evidence: R365 Employee Training; mobile delivery; standardized and customizable training; AI-powered translation; accountability and progress reporting; industry course library; food-safety certifications.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: No named Subway franchisee or confirmed rollout is supplied. The page ends by inviting readers to schedule a demo, so it may blend asserted use with prospect-oriented marketing. The archived first URL redirects to this same page and is not independent corroboration.
- Recommended follow-up: Find a named Subway franchisee case study, testimonial, implementation record, or operator statement before raising confidence or treating Restaurant365 as a Subway-wide standard.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: The two archived Restaurant365 Subway URLs are independent evidence sources.
- Pages checked: https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/restaurant-software-for-subway-franchisees/ and https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/how-subway-franchisees-are-building-stronger-teams-with-r365/
- Result: The first redirects to the second. They represent one source, not corroboration.

- Candidate or claim: Domino's or its largest franchisee uses Crunchtime based on the archived operational-consistency blog URL.
- Pages checked: https://www.crunchtime.com/blog/3-ways-dominos-largest-franchise-promotes-operational-consistency
- Result: The archived URL returns 404. No page content was available to validate product, franchisee identity, scope, or current state.

- Candidate or claim: Crunchtime's Domino's registration thank-you page establishes a customer relationship.
- Pages checked: https://www.crunchtime.com/thank-you-dominos
- Result: The live page contains generic Crunchtime navigation and registration-confirmation framing but no Domino's, franchisee, product, deployment, or testimonial content in the retrieved body. The title alone is insufficient evidence.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/restaurant-software-for-subway-franchisees/ | Redirected marketing URL | 2026-09-20 | Observation 1 | Redirects to the stronger-teams URL; duplicate source, not corroboration. |
| https://www.restaurant365.com/blog/how-subway-franchisees-are-building-stronger-teams-with-r365/ | Product/customer marketing page | 2026-09-20 | Observation 1 | Product-specific, present-tense use language, but no named operator or rollout; retained at 35% confidence. |
| https://www.crunchtime.com/blog/3-ways-dominos-largest-franchise-promotes-operational-consistency | Archived blog candidate | 2026-09-20 | No | Returns 404; no evidence could be validated. |
| https://www.crunchtime.com/thank-you-dominos | Registration thank-you page | 2026-09-20 | No | No substantive Domino's or deployment content in the live body. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Restaurant365 is actively targeting Subway franchisees and may have some franchisee adoption, but the candidate page alone cannot distinguish actual deployments from generalized segment marketing.
- Inference: The Crunchtime URLs may once have supported a Domino's-franchisee webinar or story, but the current pages do not preserve enough evidence to record even a low-confidence product mapping.
- No finding in this packet should be written directly to canonical account records without the normal RB review step.
